implementation_notes: The BCL already returns the errors instead of throwing: TryValidateObject(instance, new ValidationContext(instance), results, validateAllProperties: true) fills an ICollection<ValidationResult> with one entry per failed attribute and returns a bool, so the caller renders every violation at once; ValidateObject is the throwing counterpart and is the wrong call here. Implement IValidatableObject.Validate for cross-field rules, yielding all entries, and let ASP.NET Core turn the same results into a ValidationProblemDetails response.
pitfalls: The shorter overload validates only instance-level attributes; pass validateAllProperties: true or properties without a Required attribute are never checked.
Validator.ValidateObject throws ValidationException on the first failure - calling it inside try/catch to collect errors is exactly the anti-pattern this pattern replaces.
ValidationAttribute instances are cached per type and must be thread-safe; an attribute that keeps mutable state breaks under concurrent requests.
A ValidationResult carries only MemberNames plus a message, so codes and severities need a custom attribute or an IValidatableObject implementation.

variants.name: FluentValidation rule objects
variants.implementation_notes: FluentValidation builds the checks as rule objects outside the DTO: Validate(instance) returns a ValidationResult whose Errors collection holds every failure, with CascadeMode deciding whether the remaining rules for a property still run (the default Continue accumulates them). Choose it when rules need dependencies, rule sets or conditions that attributes cannot express; keep DataAnnotations when the rules are simple and should travel with the contract type.
pitfalls: CascadeMode.Stop makes a property fail fast while the default Continue keeps adding entries for it - document which behaviour the contract expects.
The validator instance is reusable and thread-safe, but rules that close over request-scoped state are not.
Mapping Errors to the API contract must preserve PropertyName, ErrorCode and Severity, or the response loses its field-level detail.
